live_github_issues.title: Reduce fragment captions during congregational hymns without suppressing spoken transitions
live_github_issues.original_body:
The installed Standard rehearsal emitted fragment captions such as “It dies a,” “Yeah,” “Uh,” and “Changing uh” after hymn 36 was announced. Process health stayed normal. No music-hold event appeared in the inspected prefix. The [rehearsal evidence](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/blob/0483f81a57a3ee689b51cda70ed0b8dc85e7926d/docs/evaluation/overnight_endurance_20260910/README.md) retains the exact outputs, source windows and runtime identity: session `20260910_043120_839144_en`, source `752ab9a`, EN→ES with Parakeet and E4B.

The current hold requires about five consecutive seconds of loud, VAD-negative audio. It is an energy/VAD heuristic, not a music classifier. The sparse logs cannot establish why the required streak did not occur. Parakeet's confidence and no-speech fields are proxies, so these fragments can pass current filters.

- Label a bounded natural hymn→speech transition and retain uncertain labels; generated captions are not references.
- Measure unwanted captions, suppressed legitimate speech and recovery at the spoken transition. Include quiet prayer and short valid EN/ES replies.
- Compare any detector or scheduling change with unchanged controls; report partial/final latency and negative results. Do not globally blacklist short words to manufacture a pass.

Until automatic handling is validated, the operator can Pause after the hymn announcement and Resume when spoken prayer or the message begins. This is a follow-up from #134; #137 owns any later human-approved corrections.

live_github_issues.title: Preserve hymn-title boundaries and theological meaning in final translation
live_github_issues.original_body:
A hymn title followed by a sentence lost its boundary in final translation. The English model input contains “Eternity Time will soon end,” but the Spanish final says “La eternidad pronto terminará.” The sentence subject changes from time to eternity. The full original input, preview and final are retained in the [rehearsal evidence](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/blob/0483f81a57a3ee689b51cda70ed0b8dc85e7926d/docs/evaluation/overnight_endurance_20260910/README.md), session `20260910_043120_839144_en`, chunk 3, source 414.592–422.592 s, installed `752ab9a` (Parakeet/E4B, EN→ES).

The record has STT confidence 0.98 and lightweight QE 1.0; neither checks this meaning error. Audio punctuation and a bilingual reference still need independent review.

- Preserve the raw STT string as a regression input. Establish the title/sentence boundary and an approved reference without rewriting original diagnostics.
- Compare raw and explicitly delimited input with identical models/settings, separating STT punctuation from translation behavior.
- Test subject, negation, names and theological meaning across existing canaries and natural EN/ES examples. Include sentences where eternity really is the subject; avoid a hard-coded word substitution.
- Report semantic changes and preview/final latency before promoting any prompt or context change.

This is a quality follow-up discovered during #134's rehearsal. Human correction and training approval remain separate under #137.

live_github_issues.original_body:
`workers.py` (the `--multiprocess` escape hatch, `dry_run_ab.py` ~L4036-4045) hardcodes the TranslateGemma structured chat template (~L245-290) and unconditionally builds a prompt cache. Since PR #171 made `gemma4` (Gemma 4 OptiQ E4B) the Mac default, running `--multiprocess` would feed an OptiQ E4B a TranslateGemma-shaped prompt.

Options: (a) route `workers.py` through `engines/translation_prompts.py::build_chat_messages` + `ensure_stop_tokens` (see the EOS issue) and skip the prompt cache for gemma4; or (b) deprecate `--multiprocess` now that MLX ≥ 0.31.2 gives thread-local streams and the in-process `max_workers=2` overlap is the production path (PR #168). Low priority; not on the latency critical path.

## Problem
`--mts` / `STARK_TRANSLATE_MLX_MTS` (Gemma 4 assistant-drafter speculative decoding) has never actually run. mlx-lm 0.31.3 has no `gemma4_assistant` model class (upstream PR ml-explore/mlx-lm#1276 is still open), so `load_mlx_gemma(MLX_DRAFT_MODEL_ID)` raises `Model type gemma4_assistant not supported` — swallowed at `dry_run_ab.py` ~L1218 — and `tools/benchmark_mlx_accel.py`'s `e4b_mts` config records `LOAD FAIL` (`metrics/mlx_accel_20260830_154923.json`).

## Plan (branch `feat/mlx-spec-mtp`)
Use mlx-optiq's `optiq.runtime.spec` (already installed, 0.4.34): `GemmaAssistantDrafter.from_pretrained(...)` + `spec_generate(...)` operate on the same mlx-lm `gemma4.Model` instance and yield per-token `from_draft` events (streamable, acceptance telemetry). New `engines/mlx_spec.py` wrapper; route `MLXGemmaEngine.translate_streaming` and `dry_run_ab.translate_mlx_streaming` through it (drop the non-streaming MTS fallback); add `e4b_mts` gamma sweep + byte-identical greedy check to the bench; probe script `tools/mts_acceptance_probe.py`.

## Gate
Identical output vs greedy; canary ≥ 7/8; medium p50 ≤ 0.85× the post-EOS-fix E4B; acceptance ≥ 30 % (llama.cpp reports 70–87 % on this drafter, so lower Metal acceptance is treated as an implementation issue to chase, time-boxed). Otherwise `mlx_mts` stays off. Drafter: `mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-assistant-bf16` (Google).

live_github_issues.title: chore(cuda): llama.cpp pin mismatch (Dockerfile b8783 vs start_server.sh b9022) — bump both for Gemma 4 MTP
live_github_issues.original_body:
`Dockerfile` L20 pins `ARG LLAMA_CPP_REF=b8783` while `start_server.sh` documents/pins build **b9022** (2026-05-04). The GHCR image therefore ships the older build on which `--flash-attn on` regressed Gemma 4 E4B by +56 % (`docs/archive/v2026.9/GEMMA_OPTIM_PHASE2.md`).

Upstream is at b10883 (2026-09-09) and includes Gemma 4 MTP drafter support (E2B/E4B assistants, PR #24282, 2026-06-08; fix 2026-09-01) and further Gemma 4 attention work.

Proposed: bump both pins to the same tag (≥ b10883), rebuild the GHCR image, and re-run the v2026.9 `-fa on` experiment (5 minutes) plus the MTP bench. Part of the CUDA latency proposal; needs the WSL/A2000 box.

live_github_issues.title: Preserve hymn-title boundaries and theological meaning in final translation
live_github_issues.original_body:
A hymn title followed by a sentence lost its boundary in final translation. The English model input contains “Eternity Time will soon end,” but the Spanish final says “La eternidad pronto terminará.” The sentence subject changes from time to eternity. The full original input, preview and final are retained in the [rehearsal evidence](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/blob/0483f81a57a3ee689b51cda70ed0b8dc85e7926d/docs/evaluation/overnight_endurance_20260910/README.md), session `20260910_043120_839144_en`, chunk 3, source 414.592–422.592 s, installed `752ab9a` (Parakeet/E4B, EN→ES).

The record has STT confidence 0.98 and lightweight QE 1.0; neither checks this meaning error. Audio punctuation and a bilingual reference still need independent review.

- Preserve the raw STT string as a regression input. Establish the title/sentence boundary and an approved reference without rewriting original diagnostics.
- Compare raw and explicitly delimited input with identical models/settings, separating STT punctuation from translation behavior.
- Test subject, negation, names and theological meaning across existing canaries and natural EN/ES examples. Include sentences where eternity really is the subject; avoid a hard-coded word substitution.
- Report semantic changes and preview/final latency before promoting any prompt or context change.

This is a quality follow-up discovered during #134's rehearsal. Human correction and training approval remain separate under #137.

live_github_issues.title: Reduce fragment captions during congregational hymns without suppressing spoken transitions
live_github_issues.original_body:
The installed Standard rehearsal emitted fragment captions such as “It dies a,” “Yeah,” “Uh,” and “Changing uh” after hymn 36 was announced. Process health stayed normal. No music-hold event appeared in the inspected prefix. The [rehearsal evidence](https://github.com/wrbell/stark-translate/blob/0483f81a57a3ee689b51cda70ed0b8dc85e7926d/docs/evaluation/overnight_endurance_20260910/README.md) retains the exact outputs, source windows and runtime identity: session `20260910_043120_839144_en`, source `752ab9a`, EN→ES with Parakeet and E4B.

The current hold requires about five consecutive seconds of loud, VAD-negative audio. It is an energy/VAD heuristic, not a music classifier. The sparse logs cannot establish why the required streak did not occur. Parakeet's confidence and no-speech fields are proxies, so these fragments can pass current filters.

- Label a bounded natural hymn→speech transition and retain uncertain labels; generated captions are not references.
- Measure unwanted captions, suppressed legitimate speech and recovery at the spoken transition. Include quiet prayer and short valid EN/ES replies.
- Compare any detector or scheduling change with unchanged controls; report partial/final latency and negative results. Do not globally blacklist short words to manufacture a pass.

Until automatic handling is validated, the operator can Pause after the hymn announcement and Resume when spoken prayer or the message begins. This is a follow-up from #134; #137 owns any later human-approved corrections.
